chunks: Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Yahya al-Bajali narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Uwana Musa ibn Yusuf al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yahya, from Abu Hafs, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

I was sitting in the Sacred Mosque with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when two men from the people of Basra came to him and said to him: O son of Allah's Messenger, we wish to ask you about a matter. He said to them: Ask about what you have come for. They said: Inform us about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then We made the Book an inheritance to those whom We chose from Our servants. And among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who precedes in good deeds by Allah's permission. That is the great bounty." Until the end of the two verses.

He said: It was revealed concerning us, the Household. Abu Hamza said: Then I said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, who is the one who wrongs himself? He said: The one whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal among us, the Household, he is the one who wrongs himself. I said: Who is the moderate among you? He said: The one who worships Allah, his Lord, in both conditions (life and death), until certainty comes to him. I said: Then who is the forerunner in good deeds among you? He said: The one who calls by Allah to the path of his Lord, enjoins good, forbids evil, is not a supporter to the misleaders, nor an adversary to the traitors, and is not pleased with the rule of the sinners except for he who fears for himself and his religion and finds no assistants.

key_terms.ظَالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ: One who wrongs himself (having equal good and bad deeds)

ai.seo_question: What do the terms 'wronging himself', 'moderate', and 'forerunner' mean in Surah Fatir 35:32 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly identifies the three spiritual tiers in Surah Fatir as referring to the Ahl al-Bayt, establishing their unique ontological status. The classification delineates the 'wrongdoer' as one whose merits and demerits balance out, the 'moderate' as the consistent worshipper, and the 'forerunner' as the active caller to God who embodies justice and avoids being a staunch supporter of the unjust. This exegesis highlights the Ahl al-Bayt's role not just as passive inheritors of knowledge, but as active agents of divine guidance and moral authority.
